timeline.label: Aid suspended over the Jordan canal works (Oct 1953)

Arms deliveries resume after the Ford-Rabin talks
Memorandum suspended after the Golan Heights Law (Dec 1981)

usa.agenda: Washington backs Israel's security and pressed it over nuclear inspection, settlements and arms sales to third countries (FRUS 1968; CRS).

timeline.label: Moscow breaks off relations after the legation bomb (Feb 1953)
Relations severed after the Six-Day War
Strain after the Il-20 was downed (Sept 2018)

ussr.agenda: Moscow recognised Israel in 1948, armed the Arab states from 1955, broke off relations in 1967 and restored them in 1991; from 2015 it coordinated with Israel over Syria.

timeline.label: Arms and the Dimona reactor agreement (1957)
De Gaulle's embargo after the Six-Day War; total after the Beirut raid (1968-69)
Mitterrand's state visit, the first by a French president (March 1982)
Sarkozy at the Knesset: friendship, and a call for concessions to the Palestinians (June 2008)

france.agenda: France was Israel's main arms supplier and nuclear partner from the mid-1950s until de Gaulle's embargo after June 1967.

timeline.label: De facto recognition; first Israeli envoy in London (Apr 1949)
Arms ban after the Lebanon war (June 1982)

uk.agenda: Britain recognised Israel in 1949, sold Centurion tanks and weighed Arab opinion: it withdrew the Chieftain deal in 1969 and banned arms sales from 1982 to 1994.

west_germany.agenda: Bonn paid reparations from 1952 and sent arms in secret before relations in 1965; reunified Germany later financed submarines.

eec_eu.agenda: The Community traded with Israel under successive agreements (1964, 1975, 1995/2000) and pressed it on the Palestinian question (Venice 1980; 2013 funding guidelines).

timeline.label: Israel withdraws from Sinai; UNEF on the line (1957)
Cold peace: Egypt's ambassador recalled after Sabra and Shatila (1982-86)
Ambassadors again after the Alexandria summit (1986): a cold peace
Egyptian gas for Israel and the QIZ factories: warmer trade (2004-05)
Mubarak resigns; Egypt's army says it will honour the treaty (Feb 2011)
Rioters storm the embassy in Cairo; a skeleton staff stays (Sept 2011)
Egypt cancels the gas supply deal (Apr 2012); the treaty holds
Israeli gas flows to Egypt (Jan 2020): a working peace

egypt.agenda: Egypt fought Israel four times, then made the first Arab peace in 1979; gas trade and security ties followed.

timeline.label: Ceasefire lines on the Jordan; no peace (Khartoum)
Madrid and the Washington talks: a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation (1991)
Peace treaty (26 Oct 1994), signed without a Palestinian track: a cooler peace
Peace treaty (26 Oct 1994), signed after your cabinet's hold-out over Hamas and Jerusalem: a cooler peace

jordan.agenda: Jordan's King Hussein kept a secret channel to Israel for decades before the 1994 peace; water and gas tie the two states together.

timeline.label: Madrid talks and the Syrian track (1991-2000)
Talks broken off after the Geneva summit (Mar 2000)
Revolt against Assad; a quiet ceasefire line, technically still at war (from 2011)

syria.agenda: Syria fought Israel in 1948, 1967, 1973 and 1982 and never made peace; indirect talks came and went.

timeline.label: Security zone in the south; no relations (1985-2000)
Madrid and the Washington talks; the security zone stays (1991)
Israel leaves south Lebanon; Hezbollah on the border (2000)

lebanon.agenda: Lebanon signed the 1949 armistice; war came through Lebanese territory in 1978, 1982 and 2006; a maritime border was agreed in 2022.

iraq.agenda: Iraq fought in 1948 and never signed an armistice.

timeline.label: Oil, the pipeline and Project Flower (1970s)
The Islamic Republic cuts all ties (Feb 1979)
President Ahmadinejad's call against Israel (Oct 2005) and the nuclear standoff
The nuclear deal (JCPOA), which Israel's government opposed (July 2015)
The US leaves the nuclear deal (May 2018): open hostility

iran.agenda: Under the Shah, Iran was a quiet partner of Israel's 'periphery' (oil, the Eilat-Ashkelon pipeline, Project Flower); the Islamic Republic cut all ties in 1979.

timeline.label: Mutual recognition and the Oslo Accords (1993)
No recognition: your cabinet kept to the Washington talks (1993)
The Second Intifada: the talks collapse (2000)
Abbas leads the PLO after Arafat; talks on and off (2004)

plo.agenda: The PLO, founded in 1964, waged armed struggle and won Arab recognition as the Palestinians' representative; it recognised Israel in 1993.

timeline.label: Self-rule on the map, but no agreements with your government (1994)
Oslo arrangements and security coordination; talks on and off
Abbas elected (2005); still no agreements with your government

palestinian_authority.agenda: The Palestinian Authority (1994) administers Palestinian towns under the Oslo agreements; Israel collects its customs revenue and coordinates security with it.

timeline.label: Understandings after Operation Accountability (July 1993); fighting in the security zone, no recognition
Operation Grapes of Wrath (April 1996); fighting in the security zone goes on
Israel leaves south Lebanon; Hezbollah on the border (2000)
Ceasefire under UNSCR 1701 (Aug 2006); deterrence on the border, no recognition
Western group membership in New York (2000)
Crisis after the flotilla raid; ties downgraded (2011)

turkey.agenda: The first Muslim-majority state to recognise Israel (1949); a secret periphery partner, a military partner in the 1990s, then crises from 2010.

timeline.label: Saudi airspace opened to Israeli flights (July 2022)

saudi_arabia.agenda: Saudi Arabia never had relations with Israel; it sponsored the Arab Peace Initiative of 2002.

timeline.label: Abraham Accords: peace and full normalisation (Sept 2020)

uae.agenda: The UAE normalised relations in 2020 and signed a free trade agreement in 2022.

timeline.label: Trade offices agreed during Peres's Gulf tour (April 1996)
The Arab League asks members to close their offices in Israel; Qatar's stays open (Oct 2000)
Qatar cuts its trade ties over the Gaza offensive (Jan 2009)
Liaison offices in Rabat and Tel Aviv (1994)

morocco.agenda: King Hassan II hosted secret Israeli-Egyptian contacts in 1977; liaison offices opened after Oslo and closed in 2000; relations were restored in 2020.

timeline.label: Israel recognised the PRC (1950); no relations
Liaison office of the Israel Academy in Beijing (1990)

china.agenda: Israel recognised the People's Republic in 1950; relations came only in 1992, then trade, investment and US objections to arms sales.

timeline.label: Recognition (1950) without full relations; an Israeli consulate in Bombay

india.agenda: India recognised Israel in 1950 but established full relations only in 1992; arms and agriculture made it a major partner.
